transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me a little bit about what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Well, what brought me in is... I guess I've been having some trouble with my eating habits lately. 

After my evening class, I sometimes stop for food on the way back, and I just end up eating a lot. I'll get a full fast-food meal, then grab some candy from the vending machine, and even after that, I'll eat more snacks when I finally get home. It's almost like... I don't know, like I'm trying to make up for the whole day all at once.
After these episodes of eating, do you do anything to try to compensate for the calories, such as making yourself throw up, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?

Well, yeah, I have. A few times after those late-night eating spells, I've gone into the bathroom and made myself throw up. I just... I get really scared that all that extra food is going to show on me, you know? I haven't used laxatives or tried to exercise a bunch or anything like that, but I have made myself sick a couple of times.
During those times when you eat a large amount of food, do you feel like you are unable to stop eating or cannot control how much you are consuming?

Yeah, I'd say so. Once I start on those snacks, I keep telling myself to just close the bag and go to bed. But... I don't know, my hands just keep reaching for more. I can't seem to stop until I feel embarrassed and just sick of myself.
Over the past three months, how many times on average per week have you engaged in this behavior of making yourself vomit after eating?

Well, for about the past three months, I'd say... it's usually been at least one night each week. Yeah, about once a week after my class, I end up overeating like that and then making myself throw up afterward.
